units.text: When Support Matters More Than Checking the Idea

A book about evaluation must not suggest that every mental health problem is solved by a better argument. When someone is distressed or losing the ability to distinguish interpretation from reality, safety and care may take priority over perfecting a debate. [12]

A marked change in sleep, confusion, disorganized behavior, deteriorating functioning, or very intense beliefs dominating life justify seeking professional assessment. These signs are insufficient for self-diagnosis and must not be used to label a colleague or relative. [12]

In a supportive conversation, acknowledge the experience without confirming an ungrounded explanation. One possible formulation: “I can see this experience matters a great deal and feels overwhelming. I cannot confirm the interpretation based on the chatbot’s answers. I would like us to find support together from someone qualified.” This is a communication example, not a therapeutic protocol.

Where appropriate and with respect for privacy, preserve information useful to the clinician about sleep, context, and how use has developed. Do not let a model decide on a treatment change. In situations of immediate danger, contact local emergency services. Early help can matter; the person need not prove to themselves that their distress is “serious enough” to ask for support. [12]
